column1: # Cores somebody has RUN ON A PLAYSTATION 4, and what happened. ps4/make-site.py reads this and
# shows it on cores.prx0.com; nothing else does.
# ⚠ A ROW HERE IS AN OBSERVATION ON THE CONSOLE, NOT A BUILD RESULT. "It links", "it is in the
# index" and "create-fself accepted it" are all true of cores that died on their first frame -
# swanstation was all three for a week. A core goes in only when a run is written down somewhere a
# reader can check, and the last column says where. No row means untested, and the page says so.
# Columns, tab-separated (runs of tabs are fine):
#   status     plays | slow | boots | broken - the vocabulary of ps4/CORE-STATUS.md
#                plays   content runs and is playable
#                slow    runs, below full speed - the figure goes in the note
#                boots   loads and responds, no game recorded
#                broken  loads and then fails - say how in the note
#   note       one short public sentence: the game, the frame rate. "-" for none
#   evidence   where the run is recorded. HANDOFF.md is ps4-mesa-docs/docs/retroarch/HANDOFF.md,
#              the rest are in this directory. Not shown on the page.
# ⚠ THE TESTED BUILD IS NOT ALWAYS THE PUBLISHED ONE. Cores are rebuilt from upstream's tip on
# every run, so a verdict describes the binary that was on the console that day. A regression
# shows up as a changed verdict here, not as a silent one on the page.
